title: Finite projection square from the refinement-law clause
statement: For a positive finite coefficient level, assume the refinementLaw clause for every compactification refinement, bounded-constructible source object and finite-Tor target object. Then the fixed-scalar finiteLaw projection square holds for the retained origin witnesses and target presentation.

source.place: Compactification-independence sentence; intermediate assembly from refinementLaw to finiteLaw.

proof.text: For each input of finiteLaw, package its fixed-scalar K with the supplied bounded-constructibility proof and its L with the supplied finite-Tor proof. Instantiate the assumed refinementLaw on d to c1 and d to c2, retaining O with the identity presentation and OT with the specified presentation e.

Apply the proved private categorical cancellation identity: from p;v=F(s);q and p;w=F(t);r, precompose by the isomorphism F(s), cancel v with its inverse, and use functoriality to obtain q;(v inverse;w)=F(s inverse;t);r. Use F=(- tensor L), the two theta comparisons at K, and the two theta comparisons at K tensor Lf*L.

Expand only the witnessed theta transports. At K the identity mapIso factors cancel. At the tensor object, the common-source mapIso(e) and mapIso(e inverse) cancel by functoriality. The remaining transports are exactly rhoK and rhoT of finiteLaw, with the original projection components.

proof_origin.place: M9: compactification-independence sentence, explicit common-refinement categorical cancellation and cancellation of retained witness transports. Uses the assumed refinement-law clause directly, without invoking finite_descent.

from.place: Compactification-independence sentence: compatibility of refinement comparisons with the counits and j_!, together with naturality.
